automatic_writers.note: Writers that are part of the product. A lane controller or a supervised guard joins this list when its design ships. config_sources names a writer by config_audit.source when its actor also writes by hand: metal-box-stop-loop is the box stop loop, which runs as the systemd unit virev-box-stop.service since Crawler VP p173 closed on 10-16 00:40Z, while actor metal also writes by hand from source metal-owner. canary-roster is the engage canary roster refill (crawler-v3 canary_roster.py), which keeps the roster at the owner's 10% of active accounts. hold-expiry is the rate-controller role writing a guard switch such as supply_hold.enabled back on when the end its hand switch-off carried has come (crawler-v3 hold_expiry.py, F18). rate-controller is the prod lane rate controller, F1's design, which made 544 of the 588 F1 rows in the 24 h to 10-19 15:40Z after the Crawler VP closed p170 at 15:15Z.

faults.title: The feeder's fixed high water outlasts the lease TTL on a slow platform, so feeder.high_water is lowered by hand
faults.owner: YouTube index gaps chat (01a14b8d), job youtube crawl restart (01a14bc0): on prod land 38 the feeder filled each platform to the fixed 20,000 feeder.high_water, YouTube drained about 1,200 an hour, the leases passed the 6 h FEEDER_LEASE_TTL_S, and the stale tasks blocked the feeder from 18:32Z to 22:05Z on 10-18, so the job wrote feeder.high_water 300 (audit 14445, 22:08Z) and 1800 (audit 14455, 22:27Z). 5f94dc375b sizes each platform's buffer to FEEDER_BUFFER_S (30 min) of its measured drain, 69e079b37f compares it with the feeder's own leases instead of the topic lag, and 3a27e95f4a floors it at crawl.concurrency, all in land 39 and on staging, so no buffer outlasts the lease TTL once a promote puts them on prod (prod runs land 38, 43490e7e9f, since 10-18 12:31Z). The 1800 row can stay: prod crawled 764 YouTube, 900 TikTok and 22,639 Instagram candidates in the hour to 10-19 15:10Z, so it caps only Instagram, at about 5 min of its drain, refilled every 2 s FEEDER_TICK_S, and nobody needs to write feeder.high_water by hand again

faults.title: us-metal01 runs CPU-saturated, so jobs pull media CPU levers such as media.webp_method by hand
faults.owner: ops guy chat (01a11af8), step p438, job metal01 cpu (01a154a4) with its child p438-signer-restart: us-metal01 reads 92 to 99% busy (iowait idle) since about 10-18 11Z and estate-cpu-saturated fires since 10-19 06:18Z; at 15:40Z on 10-19 it read 99.2% busy with CPU PSI some 58%, led by prod crawler-worker 13.9 CPUs, prod ClickHouse 9.2, the 12 media containers 13.6 and the 8 TikTok signers about 12. The job wrote media.webp_method 0 (audit 14865, 15:28Z) to cut libwebp CPU, but prod has run method 0 since the 2026-08-17 bench (audit 4103), so the write changed nothing and that lever is spent. The CPU fix is p438: 3c803ce5db drops the curl_cffi per-session timer of the 13 census processes from 10 Hz to 1 Hz (1,700 idle sessions 0.352 to 0.038 cores, about 3 CPUs on prod), and the signer job swaps the Chromium relaunch every 14 s for a fresh context. Once those are on prod nobody needs to write media.* encode settings by hand

exempt.note: An owner order quoted in the reason or opened with 'Owner order', or a named A/B experiment with its restore, is a decision, not a hand fix, and so is the restore row of a named live-ab window (audit 14869, proxy.connect_racers back to 20 after live-ab W1 on 10-19). The staging `.venv/bin/python - 3600 8` exec and the prod `python -c "$0"` exec of the script that opens 'Daily B2 version inventory for ONE bucket' are the declared unit virev-b2-inventory.service (host.yml --tags b2-inventory, its timer; on prod run-inventory.sh calls inventory.py host influencer-prod virev-prod-crawler-worker, read 10-18 05:34Z), so neither is a hand-started process. A board note on a d3 run or the d3 precheck reports this duty's own work, not a hand fix. A reason that quotes the owner's dated order (the owner's order of 2026-10-13: 'can we not enrich for now?', pause.enrich audit 14089) is the same kind of decision.
